nodes.question: What is the definition of environmental observers according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Environmental observers are individuals who purposely observe the environment and environmental information as part of their work or role in society.
nodes.paragraph: Human Ecology https://doi.org/10.1007/s10745-25-580-2 Introduction Climate change and biodiversity loss are impacting people on a global scale. Although the effects of environmental crises on emotions have been studied using other terms (e.g., emotional impacts of environmental issues), eco-anxiety and eco-grief have only recently been acknowledged in academic literature (Pihkala, 2022 ). There is no formally defined mental health disorder or diagnosis to describe the emotions that are associated with an awareness of ecological loss. However, these emotional states have been described as both complex and complicated (Menning, 2017 ; Sideris, 2020) ), including feeling paralyzed, daunted, or numb, and have been connected to acute and chronic mental illnesses (Bourque & Cunsolo, 2014 : Cunsolo & Ellis, 2018 ). We applied the concept of environmental observers as people who purposely observe the environment and environmental information as part of their work or role in society (e.g., Hupp et al., 2015 ; Jones et al., 2023 ). Examples of environmental observers include volunteers and employees of environmental organizations, individuals Melanie Zurba melanie.zurba@dal.ca 1 School for Resource and Environmental Studies (SRES), Dalhousie University, 6100 University Ave, PO BOX 15000, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2, Canada 2 Faculty of Health, Dalhousie University, 5968 College Street, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2, Canada 3 Department of Biology and Centre for Forest Interdisciplinary Research, The University of Winnipeg, 515 Portage Ave, Winnipeg, MB R3B 2E9, Canada 4 Division of Fine Arts, NSCAD University, 5163 Duke St, Halifax, NS B3J 3J6, Canada 5 College of Nursing, Rady Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Manitoba, 89 Curry Place, Winnipeg, MB R3T 2N2, Canada 6 Department of History, Marion McCain Arts and Social Sciences Building, Dalhousie University, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2, Canada 7 Faculty of Nursing, University of New Brunswick, 55 Lutz Street, Moncton, NB E1G 1M2, CanadaAbstract This research aimed to contribute to understanding emotional reactions to ecological change in environmental observers, who purposely observe the environment and environmental information as part of their work or role in society (e.g., citizen scientists, environmental professionals, Indigenous knowledge keepers).
